phases.name: Slice-01 — Walking skeleton: register my own instance + round-trip one claim, CID-verified (US-SF-001 + US-SF-002)

steps.name: Thick walking skeleton: publish init → push → pull of ONE signed claim through FakeInstance with an identical recomputed CID
steps.description: WS-1, the riskiest load-bearing thread (KPI-SF-1, North Star). Force the WHOLE Rust side of the opaque transport (ADR-062) into existence end-to-end, thinnest possible. (a) TEST DOUBLE: materialize `crates/test-support/src/fake_instance.rs` — `FakeInstance`, an opaque content-addressed HTTP double mirroring ADR-062 §1 (`PUT/GET /records/:cid` verbatim + idempotent, `GET /manifest` carrying the openlore discriminator envelope, `GET /` placeholder), modeled on `FakePeerPds` (tokio listener on 127.0.0.1:0), with the `fresh` posture + `endpoint_url` / `manifest` / `stored_cids` accessors (the remaining postures land in the steps that need them). Extend `tests/acceptance/support/mod.rs` with `run_openlore_publish(env, args, &FakeInstance)` (wires `OPENLORE_PUBLISH_ENDPOINT`), `assert_instance_stores_cid`, `assert_local_claims_unchanged`. (b) PORTS: add to `crates/ports` the write-capable `PublishPort` and the READ-ONLY `InstanceReadPort` (no write method — DDD-8 capability split) + boundary ADTs (manifest entry display projection, instance kind, round-trip verdict) + probe-refusal reasons `publish.instance_unreachable` / `publish.cid_roundtrip_failed` / `publish.not_an_openlore_instance`. (c) PURE CORE: NEW crate `crates/publish-domain` (Q-SF-D6 resolved = separate crate, per DESIGN recommendation) holding the pure decisions: manifest-marker classification (Q-SF-D5), display projection of a signed claim (Q-SF-D1 manifest v1), and the round-trip verdict (pushed CID vs Rust-recomputed CID). (d) DECODE REUSE: hoist the pure lexicon-JSON → SignedClaim decode into `crates/lexicon` (Q-SF-D4 resolved = hoist; it is already duplicated in adapter-atproto-pds and adapter-atproto-ingest — the hoist gives the third consumer ONE path; deduping the two existing copies is optional refactor, not required). (e) EFFECT SHELL: NEW crate `crates/adapter-publish-http` (workspace reqwest/rustls) implementing both ports against the opaque contract, with `probe()` (GET /manifest reachability + marker). (f) COMPOSITION ROOT: `crates/cli` gains the `openlore publish {init,push,pull,status}` clap group (DDD-4) — init records the target after probe; push PUTs the verbatim lexicon-JSON under the Rust-minted CID then reads it back and recomputes; pull GETs manifest + records, re-parses, recomputes via `claim-domain::compute_cid`, byte-matches, reports `1/1 verified`; status is wired minimally (asserted in 01-04). (g) ARCH: register the 2 new crates in the workspace `Cargo.toml` (21 → 23 members) and in `xtask check-arch` (publish-domain pure-core no-I/O arm; adapter-publish-http is covered by the existing only-cli-depends-on-adapters rule). (h) CM-E: WS-1 asserts via `assert_state_delta(before, after, universe, expected)` over the port-exposed universe `instance.records.cids`, `cli.publish.verified_count`, `local.claims.row_count`. Remove the WS-1 `todo!()` (it is already un-ignored).
criteria: WS-1: with one signed claim in local DuckDB and a FakeInstance registered via `openlore publish init <url>`, `openlore publish push` then `openlore publish pull` exit 0; the instance stores the verbatim record bytes under the Rust-minted CID; the pulled-back claim recomputes (in Rust claim-domain, the SOLE canonicalizer) to the IDENTICAL CID; stdout reports `1/1` verified.

WS-1 CM-E: state-delta over universe {instance.records.cids, cli.publish.verified_count, local.claims.row_count} — instance.records.cids gains exactly the one CID, verified_count == 1, local.claims.row_count UNCHANGED (additive, D-6).

`adapter-publish-http` exposes `probe()`; the publish verbs follow wire-then-probe-then-use (a failed probe refuses with a structured `health.startup.refused` carrying a publish.* reason).

steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. Functional paradigm (ADR-007): publish-domain is a pure core of total functions over ADTs (no I/O, no clocks, no randomness); all HTTP/DuckDB/FS effects live in adapter-publish-http + cli verb handlers. PBT targets in publish-domain: marker classification is total (every manifest shape classifies to exactly one instance kind); round-trip verdict is Verified iff pushed CID == recomputed CID; display projection preserves author_did/subject/predicate/object/confidence verbatim (no float rounding — include 0.0/0.5/1.0 in the generator). Hoisted decode in lexicon gets a proptest round-trip (encode→decode identity over generated SignedClaims). adapter-publish-http integration tests run against a REAL local HTTP listener (FakeInstance is a real socket server, not a mock) and cover probe fault injection: connection refused, manifest without marker, readback byte divergence. Q-SF-D1 manifest v1 (recommended): envelope {openlore:{kind:'opaque-instance', contract_version:1}, records:[{cid, author_did, subject, predicate, object, confidence, composed_at}]}; how the CLI delivers the display projection without altering the verbatim body is an OPEN DECISION (recommended: a request header carrying the projection JSON on PUT, so the Worker never parses the record body). BUILD-BEFORE-RUN: the AT spawns the `openlore` bin. Existing `[[test]]` targets for the six files are already registered in crates/cli/Cargo.toml — only add the new crate dependencies there.
steps.estimated_effort: 16h (thick WS: 2 new crates + 2 ports + test double + 4-verb group)
steps.mutation_note: Round-trip verdict (CID equality → Verified vs Mismatch) and marker classification are the load-bearing pure branches; include publish-domain + the hoisted lexicon decode in per-feature mutation testing (DV-6).

steps.name: Float gold fixture 0.0/0.5/1.0 round-trips CID-identical — acceptance mirror + the real `atproto/` Worker + publish-contract.yml CI round-trip
steps.description: RT-4 (GOLD FIXTURE, the standing guard against the REJECTED re-encode `putRecord` transport, SPIKE-00) proved at BOTH layers in one step, because they guard the same property. (a) ACCEPTANCE: add the `gold_claims_confidence_0_half_1` fixture to support and activate RT-4 — each of the three f16-representable confidences push→pull through FakeInstance with a byte-identical recomputed CID. (b) REAL WORKER (ADR-062 §1/§2, D-2): create `atproto/` — a TypeScript Cloudflare Worker + ONE Durable Object per instance: `PUT /records/:cid` stores the body VERBATIM (idempotent re-PUT = no-op success), `GET /records/:cid` returns the exact bytes or 404, `GET /manifest` returns the openlore discriminator envelope + ordered manifest entries (atomic append in the DO), `GET /` a minimal placeholder (real card in 04-01). NO `@ipld/*`, `multiformats`, or any CBOR library; the Worker computes no CID. Pinned `wrangler` + `typescript` devDependencies, `tsconfig.json` with `strict: true`, `wrangler.toml` with the DO binding, lockfile committed. (c) CI CONTRACT (DV-1, DV-2, DV-7, acceptance-review conditions #3/#4): NEW `.github/workflows/publish-contract.yml` modeled on `formula-smoke.yml` — triggers on push to main scoped to `atproto/**` + publish crates + `workflow_dispatch`; runs `npm ci`, `npx tsc --noEmit --strict`, `npm audit --audit-level=high`, starts `npx wrangler dev` (local workerd ONLY — never `wrangler deploy`, never CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN), builds `openlore`, then runs `publish init` → `push` → `pull` against the local URL (via `OPENLORE_PUBLISH_ENDPOINT`) with the 0.0/0.5/1.0 gold claims and asserts every CID matches. (d) EARNED TRUST structural layer: `xtask check-arch` gains the `atproto/` no-IPLD/CBOR dependency guard (reads `atproto/package.json` + lockfile; fails on `@ipld/*`, `multiformats`, `cbor*`).
criteria: RT-4: for each confidence in [0.0, 0.5, 1.0], a claim pushed to FakeInstance and pulled back recomputes to a byte-identical CID; all three verified.

`atproto/` Worker implements PUT/GET /records/:cid (verbatim, idempotent), GET /manifest (openlore marker envelope), GET / placeholder, backed by a single Durable Object; it contains no IPLD/CBOR/multiformats dependency and computes no CID.

`publish-contract.yml` runs `tsc --strict` and `npm audit --audit-level=high` before `wrangler dev`, then the real CLI init→push→pull round-trip including the 0.0/0.5/1.0 gold claims, failing the job on any CID mismatch; it never runs `wrangler deploy` nor references CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN.
`xtask check-arch` fails if an IPLD/CBOR/multiformats package appears in `atproto/` dependencies.

steps.name: publish init has three distinct outcomes: registered, refused-unreachable, refused-not-an-openlore-instance (Q-SF-D5)
steps.description: US-SF-001 registration contract: PI-1 (happy) + PI-2 (unreachable) + PI-4 (Q-SF-D5 discriminator). Add FakeInstance postures `unreachable` and `not_an_openlore_instance` (reachable, `/manifest` lacks the openlore marker). (PI-1) `publish init <url>` against a reachable marker-bearing instance records the target and prints instance_url + the UNCHANGED author_did + the derived card_url + the 'no central authority' confirmation (D-1/D-4). (PI-2) an unreachable URL is refused non-zero with a 'cannot reach instance' message and NOTHING is recorded (offline-first is not speculative-register). (PI-4) a reachable URL whose manifest lacks the marker is refused non-zero with 'not an openlore instance' and nothing is recorded. All three are the probe outcomes of the pure marker classification + adapter reachability, surfaced through the init verb.
criteria: PI-1: `publish init <url>` on a reachable openlore instance exits 0, records config.publish_target, prints instance_url + unchanged author_did + card_url + the no-central-authority confirmation; local.claims.row_count UNCHANGED.
PI-2: `publish init` on an unreachable URL exits non-zero with a 'cannot reach instance' message; config.publish_target stays UNSET.
PI-4: `publish init` on a reachable URL whose manifest lacks the openlore marker exits non-zero with a 'not an openlore instance' message; config.publish_target stays UNSET.
The three outcomes are distinct, greppable, and never partially register a target.
acceptance_criteria: PI-1: `publish init <url>` on a reachable openlore instance exits 0, records config.publish_target, prints instance_url + unchanged author_did + card_url + the no-central-authority confirmation; local.claims.row_count UNCHANGED.
PI-2: `publish init` on an unreachable URL exits non-zero with a 'cannot reach instance' message; config.publish_target stays UNSET.
PI-4: `publish init` on a reachable URL whose manifest lacks the openlore marker exits non-zero with a 'not an openlore instance' message; config.publish_target stays UNSET.
The three outcomes are distinct, greppable, and never partially register a target.
steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. The refusal ordering (unreachable → not-openlore → registered) is a pure decision over the probe observation; extend the publish-domain proptest so arbitrary non-marker JSON / non-JSON bodies never classify as an openlore instance. Target recording is an effect in the cli shell (config write) performed ONLY after a Registered classification — write-last, so a refusal can never leave a partial target. card_url derivation (instance_url + '/') is a pure function. adapter-publish-http integration test: real listener returning HTML at /manifest → NotOpenlore; closed port → Unreachable.
steps.mutation_note: Marker classification + write-last target recording are load-bearing; mutation must kill any change that registers on Unreachable/NotOpenlore.

steps.name: Registration never touches identity or local store, and publish status inspects the target read-only
steps.description: US-SF-001 guardrails + DDD-4 inspection: PI-3 + PI-5. (PI-3) `publish init` never makes the instance a signing authority: the author DID is unchanged, no signing key (nor seed, nor key material) is sent to the instance (assert over FakeInstance's recorded requests), and the local store is byte-unchanged (D-6/D-7). (PI-5) `openlore publish status` reports the registered instance_url, card_url, and current reachability; re-running `publish init` with a new URL re-points the target; neither touches local claims.
criteria: PI-3: after `publish init`, identity.author_did is unchanged, no request to the instance carries key material, and the local store is byte-unchanged.
PI-5: `publish status` exits 0 and prints instance_url + card_url + reachability for the registered target; local.claims.row_count UNCHANGED.
PI-5: re-running `publish init` with a different reachable URL re-points the target (status reflects the new URL) without mutating local claims.
acceptance_criteria: PI-3: after `publish init`, identity.author_did is unchanged, no request to the instance carries key material, and the local store is byte-unchanged.
PI-5: `publish status` exits 0 and prints instance_url + card_url + reachability for the registered target; local.claims.row_count UNCHANGED.
PI-5: re-running `publish init` with a different reachable URL re-points the target (status reflects the new URL) without mutating local claims.

FakeInstance gains a request log accessor (port-exposed observation of what crossed the seam) so PI-3 asserts on the boundary, not on CLI internals. Status reachability reuses the adapter probe (no new I/O path). The publish verb module must not import the signing adapter at all for init/status — keep the capability surface minimal.
steps.mutation_note: Status rendering is thin; mutation focus stays on the no-key-material boundary (any mutation that adds key material to an instance request must be killed by PI-3).

steps.name: A CID that does not survive the boundary is rejected (no silent store), and an unreachable instance never blocks offline authoring
steps.description: US-SF-002 sad paths: RT-2 + RT-3. Add FakeInstance postures `with_cid_mismatch` (stored/returned bytes diverge so the Rust recompute differs) and reuse `unreachable`. (RT-2) `publish push` detects the divergence on readback, rejects the claim as a canonicalization mismatch, reports it, exits non-zero, and the instance ends with NO record for that CID (a mismatch is a rejected sync, not a silent accept — KPI-SF-1). (RT-3) with the registered instance unreachable, `publish push` exits non-zero with 'instance unreachable', local.claims.row_count is UNCHANGED, and a subsequent `openlore graph query` succeeds offline (KPI-SF-5).
criteria: RT-2: against a divergent instance, `publish push` exits non-zero, reports a canonicalization mismatch for the claim, and instance.records.cids does not retain the mismatched record.
RT-3: against an unreachable instance, `publish push` exits non-zero with 'instance unreachable'; local.claims.row_count UNCHANGED.
RT-3: a subsequent `openlore graph query` exits 0 offline (authoring/query never depend on the instance).
acceptance_criteria: RT-2: against a divergent instance, `publish push` exits non-zero, reports a canonicalization mismatch for the claim, and instance.records.cids does not retain the mismatched record.
RT-3: against an unreachable instance, `publish push` exits non-zero with 'instance unreachable'; local.claims.row_count UNCHANGED.
RT-3: a subsequent `openlore graph query` exits 0 offline (authoring/query never depend on the instance).
steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. 'Nothing silently stored' on an append-only opaque store: the opaque contract has no DELETE, so the recommended realization is verify-BEFORE-commit — the CLI recomputes the CID from the exact bytes it is about to PUT and the readback is compared; on mismatch the manifest entry is never appended (manifest append is the commit point). If DELIVER finds the contract needs a compensating route, that is an ADR-062 amendment — raise it, do not add a route silently (OPEN DECISION). The mismatch verdict is the 01-01 pure round-trip verdict; add a proptest that any single-byte perturbation of the record yields Mismatch.
steps.mutation_note: The Mismatch → reject + no-commit branch is KPI-SF-1-critical; mutation must kill any change that commits the manifest entry on Mismatch.

phases.name: Slice-02 — Bulk publish push: additive, idempotent, resumable, owner-authed (US-SF-003)

steps.name: Bulk push sends only new claims, CID-verified, and never mutates the local store
steps.description: US-SF-003 happy + local-first guardrail: PP-1 + PP-4. Add `local_graph_of(n)` fixture and the FakeInstance `with_records` posture. (PP-1) with 42 local claims and an instance already holding 1, `publish push` pushes 41 and skips 1, reports `41/41` verified, and instance.records.cids grows by exactly 41. (PP-4) push NEVER mutates the local store: local.claims {row_count, cids, bytes} all unchanged (D-6). The push plan (Q-SF-D3 diff strategy) is a pure function of the local CID set and the instance manifest CID set. CM-E: migrate PP-1 and PP-4 to `assert_state_delta` over universes {instance.records.cids (append 41), cli.publish.{pushed,skipped,verified}, local.claims.row_count (unchanged)} and {local.claims.row_count, local.claims.cids, local.claims.bytes (all unchanged)}.
criteria: PP-1: local_graph_of(42) with 1 already on the instance → `publish push` exits 0, reports 41 pushed + 1 skipped + 41/41 verified; instance.records.cids grows by exactly 41.
PP-1 CM-E: state-delta over {instance.records.cids, cli.publish.{pushed,skipped,verified}, local.claims.row_count} matches expected (append 41 / 41,1,41 / unchanged).
PP-4 CM-E: state-delta over {local.claims.row_count, local.claims.cids, local.claims.bytes} is empty (push is additive-only).
The push plan is computed from manifest CIDs (one GET /manifest), not by probing each record.

PP-4 CM-E: state-delta over {local.claims.row_count, local.claims.cids, local.claims.bytes} is empty (push is additive-only).

steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. Pure push-plan in publish-domain with proptest laws: to_push ∪ skipped == local; to_push ∩ remote == ∅; skipped ⊆ remote; plan is deterministic (stable order); applying the plan then re-planning yields to_push == ∅ (idempotence law, which also pre-proves PP-2/PP-3). The local store is opened READ-ONLY in the push shell (StoreReadPort, not StoragePort) — the type makes PP-4 structural, the AT makes it behavioral. Universe entries are port-exposed only (FakeInstance accessors, CLI stdout counts, DuckDB row reads via support) — never internal struct fields.

steps.name: Re-push is idempotent and an interrupted push resumes without duplicates
steps.description: US-SF-003 idempotency edges: PP-2 + PP-3. (PP-2) with all 42 already on the instance, `publish push` reports 0 pushed + 42 skipped and instance.records.cids is UNCHANGED. (PP-3) with the instance holding 20 of 41 new claims (a mid-push interruption), re-running `publish push` pushes the remaining 21; the instance ends with 41 distinct CIDs and no CID appears twice in the manifest. Both fall out of the 02-01 pure plan + ADR-062 idempotent PUT; this step confirms them at the CLI contract and hardens the FakeInstance/Worker manifest against duplicate appends on re-PUT.

PP-3: after a 20-of-41 interruption, re-push pushes 21; instance.records.cids ends at 41 distinct CIDs with no duplicate manifest entry.
A raw re-PUT of an existing CID is a no-op success on both FakeInstance and the Worker (manifest length unchanged).

steps.name: The write path requires the owner token; pushes without it are refused and store nothing (DV-4 / Q-SF-D2)
steps.description: US-SF-003 write-auth: PP-5, landed on BOTH sides of the seam in one step so the contract job never goes red. Add FakeInstance posture `requiring_write_token(tok)`. (PP-5) `publish push` WITHOUT the token (or with a wrong one) is refused by the instance, the CLI reports 'unauthorized write', exits non-zero, and instance.records.cids is UNCHANGED; WITH the correct owner token the same push stores the records. Worker: `PUT /records/:cid` requires `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` compared against the Worker secret (constant-time compare); all GETs stay public. CI (acceptance-review condition #5): publish-contract.yml generates a git-ignored `atproto/.dev.vars` with a throwaway FIXTURE token, passes the same value to the CLI, and adds a negative check that a token-less push is refused. The token is never in the repo, `wrangler.toml`, or CI secrets.
criteria: PP-5: without (or with a wrong) owner token, `publish push` exits non-zero reporting 'unauthorized write'; instance.records.cids UNCHANGED.
PP-5: with the correct owner token, the same push stores the records.
The Worker enforces bearer auth on PUT only; GET /records, GET /manifest, GET / require no token.
publish-contract.yml uses a generated throwaway fixture token via `.dev.vars` (git-ignored) and asserts a token-less push is refused; no real Cloudflare credential is referenced.

OPEN DECISION (CLI token surface): recommended = the token is supplied via `OPENLORE_PUBLISH_TOKEN` (env; the CI/test seam) and persisted by the owner through the existing OS-keyring mechanism (never a plaintext config file); the token must never be echoed to stdout/stderr or logged. Only the write-capable PublishPort adapter reads the token — InstanceReadPort never carries it (capability split). adapter-publish-http integration test: real listener returning 401 → typed Unauthorized outcome (distinct from Unreachable).

phases.name: Slice-03 — Pull reconcile into local: additive, never silently overwrites (US-SF-004)

steps.name: In-sync pull is an additive no-op reconcile and every pulled claim recomputes an identical CID
steps.description: US-SF-004 happy + integrity: PR-1 + PR-4. (PR-1) instance and local both hold the same 42 claims → `publish pull` reports 42/42 matched, 0 overwritten, 'in sync'; local.claims.cids UNCHANGED. (PR-4) with the instance holding pushed claims including the 0.0/0.5/1.0 gold values, every recomputed CID byte-matches its stored key. Introduces the pure reconcile core in publish-domain: classifies each pulled record against the local set into Matched / New / Conflict / Rejected (recompute mismatch) and NEVER yields an Overwrite. CM-E: migrate PR-1 to `assert_state_delta` over {local.claims.cids (unchanged), cli.publish_pull.{matched, overwritten}}.
criteria: PR-1: with identical 42-claim sets, `publish pull` exits 0 reporting 42/42 matched, 0 overwritten, 'in sync'.
PR-1 CM-E: state-delta over {local.claims.cids, cli.publish_pull.{matched,overwritten}} → cids unchanged, matched 42, overwritten 0.
PR-4: every pulled record (incl. 0.0/0.5/1.0 confidences) recomputes to a CID byte-identical to its manifest key.
acceptance_criteria: PR-1: with identical 42-claim sets, `publish pull` exits 0 reporting 42/42 matched, 0 overwritten, 'in sync'.
PR-1 CM-E: state-delta over {local.claims.cids, cli.publish_pull.{matched,overwritten}} → cids unchanged, matched 42, overwritten 0.
PR-4: every pulled record (incl. 0.0/0.5/1.0 confidences) recomputes to a CID byte-identical to its manifest key.
steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. Reconcile proptest laws: the classification partitions the pulled set (matched + new + conflict + rejected == pulled); there is no Overwrite variant (make it unrepresentable in the ADT); reconcile(local, local) is all-Matched; any record whose recompute differs is Rejected, never New. The pull shell recomputes via claim-domain BEFORE classification (verify-before-trust); only New records are candidates for insert (03-02).
steps.mutation_note: Reconcile classification is the core of US-SF-004; include every arm in per-feature mutation (a Matched↔New or Rejected↔New swap must be killed).

steps.name: Fresh-machine pull rebuilds local DuckDB with attribution intact; an unreachable instance leaves local untouched
steps.description: US-SF-004 boundary + offline: PR-2 + PR-5. (PR-2) empty local store + instance holding 42 → `publish pull` inserts all 42 into local DuckDB (and their `<cid>.json`), each attributed to its author_did, each CID recomputed + verified BEFORE insert; local.claims.row_count 0 → 42. (PR-5) with the instance unreachable, `publish pull` exits non-zero with 'instance unreachable', local.claims UNCHANGED, and a subsequent `graph query` succeeds offline (KPI-SF-5).
criteria: PR-2: fresh local store → `publish pull` exits 0; local.claims.row_count goes 0 → 42, each row attributed to its author_did, each inserted only after its CID verified.
PR-5: unreachable instance → `publish pull` exits non-zero with 'instance unreachable'; local.claims UNCHANGED.
PR-5: a subsequent `openlore graph query` exits 0 offline.

Pulled records whose author_did is NOT the local identity are an open question for rebuild (own-instance should only hold own claims; the PC-5 two-author fixture shows it can hold others) — recommended: own-author records go to `claims`, foreign-author records are reported and NOT inserted into `claims` (anti-merging); confirm in this step (OPEN DECISION).

steps.name: A conflicting pulled record is surfaced, never silently overwrites the local claim
steps.description: US-SF-004 no-silent-overwrite guardrail: PR-3. A pulled record whose CID differs from a local claim's CID for the SAME logical record → `publish pull` surfaces the conflict (names both CIDs), exits non-zero, the local claim is UNCHANGED, nothing is auto-resolved. Requires the pure reconcile core to identify 'same logical record' across differing CIDs. CM-E: migrate PR-3 to `assert_state_delta` over {local.claims.cids, local.claims.bytes (unchanged), cli.publish_pull.conflicts (1)}.
criteria: PR-3: `publish pull` exits non-zero and reports the conflict naming the local CID and the pulled CID.
PR-3 CM-E: state-delta over {local.claims.cids, local.claims.bytes, cli.publish_pull.conflicts} → local unchanged, conflicts == 1.
No auto-resolution: neither side is overwritten and the conflicting pulled record is not inserted.
acceptance_criteria: PR-3: `publish pull` exits non-zero and reports the conflict naming the local CID and the pulled CID.
PR-3 CM-E: state-delta over {local.claims.cids, local.claims.bytes, cli.publish_pull.conflicts} → local unchanged, conflicts == 1.
No auto-resolution: neither side is overwritten and the conflicting pulled record is not inserted.
steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. OPEN DECISION (logical-record identity): content-addressed claims have no mutable identity, so 'same logical record, different CID' needs an explicit key. Recommended: (author_did, subject, predicate, object) — a differing confidence/evidence/composed_at under that key is a Conflict. Encode the key as a pure function in publish-domain with a proptest law: two records with equal key and unequal CID always classify Conflict; equal CID always Matched.
steps.mutation_note: Conflict detection is the D-6 guardrail; mutation must kill any change that downgrades Conflict to New or Matched.

steps.name: The card renders only pushed claims, each attributed to its author DID; an empty instance renders 'no claims published yet'
steps.description: US-SF-005 happy + boundary + only-pushed guardrail: PC-1 + PC-2 + PC-3. The REAL card lives in the Worker: `atproto/src/card.ts` renders `GET /` as read-only HTML from the manifest display projection (the data the real CLI wrote on push) — one row per manifest entry attributed to its author_did, no authoring/edit control, no merged row; an empty manifest renders a 200 'no claims published yet' page. FakeInstance's `card_html` mirrors the same card contract for the acceptance layer. (PC-1) after pushing claims, GET / lists each pushed claim attributed to its author_did with no authoring control and no consensus row. (PC-2) FakeInstance::fresh → 200 'no claims published yet', zero rows, not an error. (PC-3) a local claim authored after the push and NEVER pushed is absent from the card. publish-contract.yml gains card assertions against real workerd (pushed CID rows present, attributed; empty-instance text).
criteria: PC-1: after `publish push`, GET / lists every pushed claim, each attributed to its author_did; no authoring/edit control; merged_count == 0.
PC-2: on a fresh instance GET / returns 200 with 'no claims published yet' and zero rows.
PC-3: a local claim that was never pushed does not appear on the card.
The real Worker `GET /` satisfies the same contract under publish-contract.yml (live workerd).

PC-2: on a fresh instance GET / returns 200 with 'no claims published yet' and zero rows.

steps.implementation_notes: Test paradigm: acceptance = example-based via CLI subprocess driving port; pure domain = property-based (proptest); adapters = real-infrastructure integration tests, never mocked. Honest boundary: at the acceptance layer the production code under test is the CLI-written manifest display projection (real push); the FakeInstance card render is a contract mirror, so the REAL render MUST be asserted in publish-contract.yml against workerd in this same step — otherwise PC-1..3 only test the double. Card HTML must escape every manifest field (the projection is attacker-controllable by anyone who can write — i.e. the owner — but viewers are the public; XSS-safe by construction). Card render is TS; no Rust pure logic added (the display projection PBT from 01-01 covers the Rust side).
steps.mutation_note: No new Rust logic; the Rust-side guarantee is the display projection (01-01 mutation scope). TS card mutation is out of scope (DV-6).

steps.name: The card is write-incapable, never merges two authors into one row, and reads need no token
steps.description: US-SF-005 guardrails: PC-4 + PC-5 + PC-6. (PC-4) the card offers no authoring/write control and the read surface exposes NO write method — Earned Trust structural layer lands here: `xtask check-arch` gains `publish_write_capability_isolated` (source-scan rule in the pubkey/viewer-seam pattern): only the `openlore publish` verb module may construct/wire the write-capable PublishPort adapter; `verbs/peer_pull.rs` and any card/read path must not reference it. (PC-5) identical claim content pushed under two distinct author_dids (two TestEnv identities, same instance) renders as TWO attributed rows, merged_count == 0 (KPI-SF-3, anti-merging). (PC-6) with `requiring_write_token(tok)`, GET / and GET /manifest WITHOUT a token both return 200 (DV-4 asymmetry — the PP-5 counterpart).
criteria: PC-4: the card exposes no authoring/write control, and `xtask check-arch` fails if any non-publish verb or read path references the write-capable publish adapter/port.
PC-5: identical claims from two author DIDs render as two rows, each attributed to its own DID; merged_count == 0.
PC-6: GET / and GET /manifest succeed without any token on a write-token-protected instance.

phases.name: Slice-05 — Cross-instance federated read: peer pull from another user's instance (US-SF-006, J-003 transport delta)

steps.name: peer pull reads a peer's Cloudflare instance via the opaque read, verifies locally, and stores into peer_claims without merging
steps.description: US-SF-006 happy + anti-merging + verify-before-trust: CI-1 + CI-4 + CI-5. The J-003 `peer add` / `peer pull` flow is REUSED verbatim; the ONLY delta is transport: when a peer's resolved serviceEndpoint is an opaque openlore instance, `peer pull` reads `GET /manifest` + `GET /records/:cid` through the READ-ONLY InstanceReadPort, recomputes each CID in Rust from the returned bytes, verifies the signature with the J-003 machinery, and stores into `peer_claims` attributed to the peer — never into the reader's own claims. Test wiring: a peer FakeInstance for did:plc:rachel-test, resolver seam `OPENLORE_PEER_PDS_ENDPOINT_<did>` pointed at it, subscription via the REAL `peer add`. (CI-1) 7 records, 5 new → 5/5 verified and stored attributed to Rachel. (CI-4) author_claims {row_count, cids} unchanged; no row attributed to a DID other than its true author. (CI-5) each stored record's CID was recomputed from the returned bytes and byte-matched before insert. CM-E: migrate CI-1 and CI-4 to `assert_state_delta` over {peer_storage.claims.row_count_by_author[rachel] (+5), author_claims.row_count (unchanged), author_claims.cids (unchanged)}. Extend the 04-02 `publish_write_capability_isolated` guard to assert peer_pull wires ONLY InstanceReadPort.
criteria: CI-1: `openlore peer pull` against a peer instance with 7 records (5 new) exits 0; 5/5 verified (signature + recomputed CID); 5 rows land in peer_claims attributed to did:plc:rachel-test.
CI-1/CI-4 CM-E: state-delta over {peer_storage.claims.row_count_by_author[rachel], author_claims.row_count, author_claims.cids} → +5 / unchanged / unchanged.
CI-4: no pulled row is attributed to a DID other than its true author; nothing is merged into the reader's own claims.
CI-5: every stored peer record's CID was recomputed in Rust from the returned bytes and byte-matched its manifest key before insert.
The peer-pull path holds no write capability toward the peer instance (InstanceReadPort only; check-arch enforced).
acceptance_criteria: CI-1: `openlore peer pull` against a peer instance with 7 records (5 new) exits 0; 5/5 verified (signature + recomputed CID); 5 rows land in peer_claims attributed to did:plc:rachel-test.

OPEN DECISION (transport selection): a peer serviceEndpoint may be a classic PDS (existing XRPC path) or an opaque instance. Recommended: probe `GET /manifest` for the openlore marker (reuse the 01-01/01-03 pure marker classification) — marker present → InstanceReadPort path; absent → existing PdsPort path unchanged (so all shipped peer_pull ATs stay green). The selection is a pure function over the probe observation (proptest: every observation maps to exactly one transport). Reuse the hoisted lexicon decode + J-003 verify/attribution verbatim — no second verify path. Run the full existing peer_* acceptance suite as a regression gate for this step.
steps.mutation_note: Transport selection + verify-before-insert on the opaque read are load-bearing; mutation must kill a change that routes a marker-bearing endpoint to the XRPC path or inserts before recompute.

steps.name: A tampered peer claim is rejected while valid ones are stored; an unreachable peer instance is skipped while others proceed
steps.description: US-SF-006 sad paths: CI-2 + CI-3 — J-003 fault semantics carried over to the opaque transport. (CI-2) a peer instance whose record set includes one tampered signature → that record is rejected + reported, the honest records land in peer_claims, exit non-zero (KPI-FED-6 discipline). (CI-3) two subscribed peers, one reachable instance and one `FakeInstance::unreachable()` → the unreachable peer is skipped + reported, the reachable peer's claims are stored, exit non-zero overall (per-peer fault isolation).
criteria: CI-2: the tampered record is rejected and reported; the valid records are stored in peer_claims; exit non-zero.
CI-3: the unreachable peer instance is skipped and reported; the reachable peer's claims are stored; exit non-zero overall.
Neither fault aborts the whole pull nor stores an unverified record.
